{{Quote|You gotta love the Z-95. Nothing beats the feeling of power they give you.|A [[Bandit Squadron]] [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]]|<ref name="XWA" />}}
The '''Z-95 Headhunter''' was a [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighter]] designed jointly by [[Incom Corporation/Legends|Incom]] and [[Sublight Products Corporation|Subpro Corporations]] [[Standard year/Legends|years]] before the [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|Invasion of Naboo]]. Its resilience and longevity meant it remained a staple of private and low-priority government starfighter forces long after its introduction.

==Characteristics==
{{Quote|As long as they keep on making upgrades for this baby, the Z-95 will never become outdated.|[[Outlaw tech/Legends|Outlaw tech]] [[Klaus Vandangante/Legends|Klaus "Doc" Vandangante]]|<ref name="NEGVV" />}}
[[File:Z95headhunter_egvv.jpg|thumb|left|180px|Z-95-AF4 Headhunter [[:Category:Technical drawing images|schematics]]]]
Considered one of the most capable fighters of its day, it boasted a distinctive bubble canopy and a set of [[Triple blaster/Legends|triple blasters]] mounted at the ends of each of its two variable geometry wings; later versions dispensed with the swing wings and bubble canopy in favor of more precise maneuvering thrusters and canopy instrumentation. Its sleek yet rugged design was attributed to [[Seti Ashgad/Legends|Seti Ashgad]], a [[Scientist/Legends|scientist]] in Incom's [[Hyperdrive Design Division]].

It was named after the [[Coromon Headhunter/Legends|Coromon headhunter]], a predator native to the [[Coromon Islands]] on [[Fresia/Legends|Fresia]], the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] where Incom was headquartered.

The Z-95 was smaller in size than its successors: the Incom/Subpro [[Aggressive ReConnaissance-170 starfighter/Legends|ARC-170]], designed during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], the [[Clone Z-95 starfighter/Legends|clone Z-95 starfighter]], also made in the Clone Wars, and the Incom [[T-65 X-wing starfighter/Legends|T-65 X-wing]], designed shortly before the outbreak of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]].

Though the Z-95 still enjoyed considerable use in the years following the establishment of the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]], it was clearly outclassed by fighters developed in the decades since its original release. When compared to the T-65, it was slower, less maneuverable, had lighter armor and [[Deflector shield/Legends|shielding]], and was not as heavily armed.

<div style="float:right">[[File:Z-95X.jpg|thumb|right|180px|[[Booster Terrik]]'s heavily modified Z-95 Headhunter equipped with [[T-65 X-wing starfighter/Legends|X-wing]]-style [[S-foils/Legends|S-foils]]]]</div>
It was fairly inexpensive and reliable, making it a favorite amongst [[Smuggler/Legends|smugglers]], [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]] organizations, local system defense forces, and bright-eyed youngsters with dreams of becoming fighter jockeys. Pirate groups such as the [[Nebula Front/Legends|Nebula Front]] also used the Z-95. Also, despite the later T-65 being more maneuverable, the Z-95 was known to be able to perform a tighter turn.

Owing to its longevity, it was not surprising that many variants of the Z-95 came into existence due to the efforts of starship mechanics and hotrod [[Pilot/Legends|pilots]] throughout [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]]; these included a split-wing version, a courier version that could accommodate a single passenger, variants with various alternative weapons loadouts, and a trainer version, the [[Z-95XT Trainer]], that was commonly used by the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] until replaced by the T-65X, the trainer variant of the X-wing.

Later model variants had the [[Zr-390 navicomputer system]] from [[Narmox]] installed.<ref name="OS" />

==History==
===Republic service===
{{Quote|Give me the choice, I'd take a Z-95 Headhunter every time.|[[Unidentified retired Galactic Republic pilot|A Galactic Republic pilot]]|<ref name="TPMnovel">[[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace (novelization)|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'' novelization]]</ref>}}
[[File:Clone_Z-95_starfighter_SWE.png|thumb|left|200px|The Republic's [[Clone Z-95 starfighter/Legends|clone Z-95 starfighter]]]]
The Z-95 was first constructed for the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] before the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]]. The prototype for the Z-95 was the ''[[Onyx Star]]'', developed at the [[Bahalian Shipyards]].

After Subpro and Incom ended their partnership, Incom reportedly bought the intellectual property rights and proprietary systems of the Z-95.

One notable Z-95 was the [[Dicer (starfighter)|''Dicer'']] flown by the [[Bothan/Legends|Bothan]] pilot [[Eelo Begraas]] around [[31 BBY/Legends|31 BBY]]. He painted it [[Color/Legends|red]]-on-black, a color scheme that was immediately identifiable to his opponents. Such was Begraas' reputation that the mere sight of the Headhunter was enough to send many opposing pilots into hysterics.<ref name="Troop Movements">{{Wizards|url=rpga/livingforce/article.asp?x=lf/swlf20011206b_troop&c=swlfc|text=Troop Movements}}</ref>

[[Nirama]], [[Organization|crimelord of the]] [[Cularin system/Legends|Cularin system]], used Z-95s both as his sponsored ships for the races of [[Eskaron]], and to provide armored transport to some of his main minions.<ref name="POB">{{LivingForce|The Price of Business}}</ref>

One year [[23 BBY/Legends|before]] the start of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Jedi Master/Legends|Master]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]], while on a [[Mission to Fondor (Separatist Crisis)|mission to Fondor]], piloted a Z-95 owned by [[Fondor/Legends|Fondor's]] [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] [[Rodd]] to infiltrate and destroy a [[Groodo]] the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]]-fabricated [[False Sun Runner|counterfeit]] of the ancient [[Corellia StarDrive]] transport, the ''[[Sun Runner]]''. While successful in the task, he was forced to retrieve his [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]] [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] who, piloting a Rodd-owned [[CloakShape fighter/Legends|CloakShape fighter]], was forced to crash-land on the [[Fondorian]] jungle-moon [[Nallastia]].<ref name="Star Wars Adventures 1: Hunt the Sun Runner">''[[Star Wars Adventures 1: Hunt the Sun Runner]]''</ref>

A Headhunter variant, the [[Clone Z-95 starfighter/Legends|clone Z-95 starfighter]], saw use during a [[Battle of Umbara/Legends|Republic campaign]] to retake the planet [[Umbara/Legends|Umbara]]. Also, Headhunters participated in the [[Outer Rim Sieges/Legends|Outer Rim Sieges]] against the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]]. After the war, the Z-95 would fall into the hands of parties other than the newly-formed [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], such as [[Pirate/Legends|pirates]] and other underworld groups.
<div style="float:right">[[File:Z-95_TCG_by_Chase_Toole.jpg|thumb|left|180px|A Z-95 taking off from a [[Spaceport/Legends|spaceport]]]]</div>

===Galactic Civil War===
Though outdated by the time of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], Z-95 Headhunters were well respected starfighters that were available to buy from various [[Merchant/Legends|merchants]], and were still in common use as late as the [[Second Galactic Civil War]].

[[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] piloted an early model Z-95 Mark I while leading the defense of an [[Outlaw tech/Legends|outlaw tech]] base in the [[Corporate Sector/Legends|Corporate Sector]] against [[Corporate Sector Authority/Legends|CSA]] [[IRD-A starfighter|IRD-A fighters]]. However, by this period, they were considered obsolete compared to other fighters.<ref name="HSatCSS">''[[Han Solo and the Corporate Sector Sourcebook]]''</ref>

The Rebellion used [[Z-95t Headhunter]]s in close air support roles.<ref name="Tala 1">{{CCG|set=Death Star II Limited|cardname=Tala 1}}</ref><ref name="Tala 2">{{CCG|set=Death Star II Limited|cardname=Tala 2}}</ref><ref name="Close Air Support">{{CCG|set=Death Star II Limited|cardname=Close Air Support}}</ref> The temporary Alliance covert squadron, [[Bandit Squadron]], also used Z-95s.<ref name="XWA" /> The [[m'Yalfor'ac Order]] in [[Guiteica/Legends|Guiteica]] was also known to use these by-then obsolete fighters around [[2 ABY/Legends|2 ABY]].<ref name="air">''[[Alliance Intelligence Reports]]''</ref> [[N'dru Suhlak]] piloted a Z-95 with an expanded cockpit to carry passengers.<ref name="Slave Ship">''[[Slave Ship]]''</ref>

[[Mara Jade Skywalker|Mara Jade]] used a [[Hyperdrive/Legends|hyperdrive]]-equipped Headhunter during the [[Thrawn campaign|Thrawn crisis]]. Her Headhunter had a single center-mounted [[Ion cannon/Legends|ion cannon]] instead of the standard [[Concussion missile/Legends|concussion missile]] launchers. [[Jaina Solo Fel|Jaina Solo's]] first ship, [[Crystal (starfighter)|''Crystal'']], was also a Z-95 Headhunter, and [[Jaden Korr]] flew a [[Hyperdrive/Legends|hyperdrive]]-equipped Headhunter named ''[[Far Wanderer]]'' on missions to different worlds such as [[Bakura/Legends|Bakura]], [[Hoth/Legends|Hoth]], and [[Korriban/Legends|Korriban]].<ref name="Star Wars: Jedi Knight: Jedi Academy">''[[Star Wars: Jedi Knight: Jedi Academy]]''</ref> Another prominent member of the New Republic to use a Headhunter was [[Tycho Celchu/Legends|Tycho Celchu]], during the reforming of Rogue Squadron; however, the armaments were significantly weakened as at the time he was considered an Imperial spy. Five Headhunters were also used to great effect in the closing stages of the [[Liberation of Coruscant (Galactic Civil War)|mission to retake Coruscant]] in [[7 ABY/Legends|7 ABY]], by [[Corran Horn/Legends|Corran Horn]], [[Erisi Dlarit]], [[Rhysati Ynr]], [[Pash Cracken/Legends|Pash Cracken]], and [[Asyr Sei'lar]]. The four Z-95s that survived the conflict&mdash;Corran's was destroyed during his capture&mdash;were sold off to various museums to raise funds for Rogue Squadron's attack on [[Thyferra/Legends|Thyferra]].

==Behind the scenes==
Although the Z-95 is a one-person ship, with [[N'dru Suhlak]]'s modified unit accepting one passenger, the [[RPGA]] adventure ''[[The Price of Business]]'' featured a Z-95 that took [[Len Markus]] and some other fifteen people from Genarius to Cularin.

In ''[[Star Wars: Empire at War]]'', the sign of the Z-95 is used to represent the [[Alpha-3 Nimbus-class V-wing starfighter/Legends|V-wing fighter]]. In ''[[Star Wars: Empire at War: Forces of Corruption]]'', this is fixed.

In the game ''[[Star Wars: Jedi Starfighter]]'', if the player enters HEADHUNT as a cheat code, the player can fly the Z-95 during missions.

For its appearance in the ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'' television series beginning with the episode "[[Darkness on Umbara]]," the Headhunter was originally designated as a separate class, the "Z-85 Headhunter." This was later rectified in the episode's [http://www.starwars.com/explore/the-clone-wars/ep407/#!/media/slideshow guide], which corrected the ship name to read simply "Headhunter," giving no indication that the Headhunter in ''The Clone Wars'' was intended to be different from the original Z-95.
